abstract: Humanized transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) mice are frequently used to evaluate blood-brain barrier (BBB) delivery, yet available strains differ in the extent and design of receptor humanization. We compared two NanoNewron NewroBus-based anti-TNF constructs, NN-841 (D3 TfR1-binding module) and NN-843 (A2 module), in JAX #038212 (humanized apical domain), Cyagen C001584 (human extracellular-domain CDS model), Cyagen C001860 (human extracellular-domain genomic replacement model), and wild-type controls. Thirty mice received intravenous injections and were evaluated 24 h later. Brain parenchymal-fraction signals were reported in all 12 Cyagen mice, but in none of six JAX or 12 wild-type animals. Serum concentrations were measurable in every group and followed the same rank order for both constructs: Cyagen-CDS>Cyagen-HU>wild type >JAX. Mean CDS-to-JAX serum ratios were approximately 13--fold for both constructs. Compared with the Cyagen-HU strain, the CDS strain showed higher parenchymal concentrations; the ratio of mean parenchymal to mean serum concentration increased prominently for NN-841, but only modestly for NN-843. These findings indicate that model choice influences 24-h circulating concentrations and apparent BBB delivery. Circulating soluble human TfR1-mediated stabilization and endothelial TfR1-dependent transport are plausible, untested explanations for strain-dependent differences. A negative brain-delivery result in JAX #038212 alone cannot be taken as evidence that NewroBus lacks BBB delivery activity
